To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MYC activity mitigates the response to rapamycins in prostate cancer through inhibition of autophagic cell death.
MYC activity mitigates the response of prostate cancer cells to rapamycin through 4EBB1-mediated inhibition of the autophagy pathway.
MYC activity is associated with resistance to rapamycin-induced autophagy, which is due to inhibition of 4EBP-mediated autophagy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of autophagy in prostate cancer and how this may be modulated to enhance the efficacy of existing therapies.
the mechanisms of resistance to cancer therapy and the role of autophagy in cancer progression and response to therapy.
understanding the role of MYC and its downstream effectors in regulating autophagy and the role of this process in tumorigenies and in response to therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
autophagy is a double-edged sword, with the balance of the autophagic response tipping towards cell death or survival, depending on the context of the tumor.
the role of autophagy is complex, and it can have both pro- and anti-tumorigenic properties.
autophagy can promote cancer progression and/or survival, but also can be an important mechanism for tumor cell death.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
autophagy is a double-edged sword for cancer cells.
MYC activity in prostate cancer cells can promote autophagy and that autophagy is critical for survival under nutrient deprivation conditions.
autophagy is a mechanism for survival in the context of prostate cancer, and that MYC can modulate this process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the balance between autophagy and apoptosis is critical in determining whether rapamycin is a pro-survival or pro-death agent in prostate cancer.
MYC activity in cancer cells is a major driver of resistance to the mTORC1 inhibitor rapamycin, and that this is mediated by 4EBP-1-mediated inhibition of the autophagic process.
MYC activity can inhibit autophagy in prostate cancer cells and that this inhibition of autophagosome-lysosome fusion can be overcome with rapamycin.
